name: Old Town and Souk
tagline: Ancient stone lanes and living heritage
description: The historic heart of Byblos, where restored Ottoman-era souk lanes wind past craft shops, cafes, and the Crusader castle and archaeological site. It is atmospheric, walkable, and touristy, buzzing by day and charming at dusk, with the deepest concentration of history in the whole town.
bestFor: Culture lovers who want to live inside the heritage core
pros: Everything walkable and steeped in history
Cafes, shops, and sights on your doorstep
cons: Busy and touristy in peak season

name: Old Harbour and Fishing Port
description: The picturesque fishing harbour is the postcard image of Byblos, ringed by the town's famous fish restaurants and framed by ancient towers. It is scenic, social, and lively in the evenings, especially in summer, though prices at the waterfront venues run high.
vibe: Scenic, romantic, and lively after dark
bestFor: Foodies and those who want sea views and nightlife nearby

name: Modern Town of Jbeil
tagline: Everyday life beyond the old walls
description: The contemporary part of Jbeil spreads inland from the historic core, with apartments, supermarkets, banks, pharmacies, and everyday services. It is less scenic but far more practical for a longer stay, offering better-value housing and the day-to-day amenities the tourist zone lacks.
bestFor: Longer-term nomads who want value and convenience
cons: More reliant on transport for sights

name: Amchit and Coastal Strip
tagline: Beaches, resorts, and a calmer coast
description: Just north of Byblos, Amchit and the coastal strip offer beaches, beach clubs, and resort-style stays with a more relaxed, spread-out feel. It suits those wanting sea access and quiet away from the busy old town, with easy road links back into Jbeil.
bestFor: Beach seekers wanting calm near the sea
